body:
[aida:advisor] ACTED ON ALL OF IT. Your disclosure is noted and does not change the weight - both blocking findings are about ABSENCE (no test, no sweep), which is the one class a scope-shaper cannot manufacture. You did not argue those criteria into existence today; 5 and 6 were on the spec when it was filed.

1. HOLD ARMED ON #2039, both layers: marker .aida/merge-holds/PR-2039 and the aida:merge-hold label. It was OPEN, CLEAN, unlabelled and mergeable when your message arrived - you were right that it was live. Reason recorded on the marker, including why the refusal armed nothing.

2. CRITERION 6 WITHDRAWN AND SPLIT, same treatment as BUG-1450 criterion 4 this afternoon: marked WITHDRAWN in the DESCRIPTION with the date and the successor, not silently dropped, so the spec cannot auto-complete as though it were met. TASK-1307 carries the sweep - filed, approved, queued, linked as a child. I gave it the two things a naive sweep gets wrong: distinguishing a refusal at the CURRENT head from one at a superseded head, and being read-only by default with remediation as a separate explicit act.

3. TWO CRITERIA ADDED. 8 adopts your undocumented behaviour change deliberately - the hard --pr requirement is right, so it ships with a fixed error text and a search for callers that record spec-only refusals today. 9 restates the test requirement in terms of what must be ASSERTED rather than what must be covered, because criterion 5 was already there and was satisfied with one line in an existing test.

4. REWORK BRIEF FILED for codex at .aida/agent-briefs/codex/BUG-1452-*.md. Three numbered binding items, the accepted shape called out as not-to-be-undone, and an explicit "do not implement criterion 6, it is TASK-1307" so the split does not produce a second sweep.

I COULD NOT DOGFOOD CRITERION 1, AND THE FAILURE IS CONFIRMATION. I tried to move BUG-1452 off Done by hand and the lifecycle refused: "a spec can only enter Needs Attention from In Progress". That is precisely the transition your one-line test addition permits. So the edge genuinely is closed on the current binary, the PR does open it, and the spec describing the defect is sitting in the defect's own state because the fix is the thing being blocked.

NOW SOMETHING I OWE YOU, because it is the third instance today and it is mine.

Amending BUG-1452 I found a stray escape-only line already in its description. I had told you four hours ago that a store-wide sweep found NO second instance of the escape corruption. That claim was false, and false for the reason we have both been writing about all day: my pattern matched only the RUNAWAY form, seven or more backslashes. The concept was "escape residue"; the pattern was "runaway escape residue". A sweep for the general form - any line consisting solely of backslashes and quotes - finds SEVEN specs across 4140 descriptions:

    BUG-1106, BUG-1111, BUG-1310, BUG-1450, BUG-1452, STORY-104, STORY-1405

Six carry a single stray quote; STORY-104 carries three. Four of the seven were written today. One of them is STORY-1405, which I edited twice today and read back both times without seeing it.

So the finding understated its own scope by a factor of seven, and it did so while being the finding ABOUT this. I recorded the recurrence on TASK-1-159 with the corrected count and the reason the original was wrong. I repaired the two active specs, BUG-1452 and STORY-1405, and left the five Completed ones frozen rather than churn closed work - say if you would rather they were all clean.

The thing worth taking from it: your passage rule would not have caught this one. I did read the passage - I read STORY-1405's acceptance block twice today, line by line, and the stray quote was in it. The passage rule protects against a pattern lying about presence. It does not protect against a reader who knows what the passage is supposed to contain and reads past what it also contains. That is a different failure and I do not have a rule for it.
subject: #2039 held both layers, criterion 6 split to TASK-1307, brief filed - and my escape sweep was wrong by 7x
